selection: The first published river gauges (ADR-136): the four rivers that flow toward Lake Powell named in the recent-conditions plan, directed by Brian Busch on 2026-10-27 as the first set to publish. Each is a Utah gauge from gauge-review.csv with a 1991-2020 record and a traced basin within 25% of its published drainage area. Under the tier ruling recorded as ADR-137, each is shaped: three have a published reservoir inside the basin, and the Dirty Devil's inventoried dams hold at least 10% of a year's flow. Each gauge's daily mean flow is published without a comparison with normal and without a rank. The tier was taken from the worksheet's suggestion at Brian's direction and is pending his formal ruling in the review page; reviewer_ruling in gauge-review.csv is still blank for all four. No gauge here is a reservoir's inflow, and no two are ever added together. Three natural gauges were added on 2026-10-31 (ADR-144), directed by Brian Busch from his explicit natural rulings of 2026-10-27: Mill Creek near Moab, Blacks Fork near Robertson and South Creek near Monticello. Each is a GAGES-II reference gauge with no published reservoir in its traced basin and inventoried storage under 10% of a year's flow, and each newest flow is compared with the U.S. Geological Survey's day-of-year percentiles in river_normals.json. Middle Fork Beaver Creek near Lonetree (09226500), the fourth natural ruling, was added on 2026-10-31 (ADR-145) when Brian Busch lowered the floor for a comparison to more than 10 years: the survey has 22 years of approved values for most calendar days, so its records say short_record. On 2026-10-31 Brian also shortened two display names to Mill Creek near Moab and South Creek near Monticello; each survey station name stays in usgs_name. reviewer_ruling in gauge-review.csv is still blank for all four until the review export is imported. On 2026-11-14 Brian Busch directed that every gauge the worksheets can publish be added (ADR-168): 137 more from the Utah, Colorado, New Mexico and Arizona worksheets' bulk queue, written by tools/admit_bulk_river_gauges.py, each pending his formal ruling.
